title: Forensics: image acquisition with dd and FTK Imager

videos.script: Thursday's data left from the file server. Which files, nobody knows yet. The answer is on its disk. {{disk}} But the disk is evidence, and evidence is only worth something if it was never changed. So nobody opens it. A copy is made, bit for bit, through something that cannot write. {{copy}} Then a hash proves the copy and the original are the same, down to the last byte. You will do it twice: with dd, which every Linux has, and in the format FTK Imager writes, with its case details inside. {{e01}} And you will write down who held the evidence, and when. That record is as much a part of it as the bytes.
